requirements.quote:
For each authoritative RRset in a signed zone, there MUST be at least
   one RRSIG record that meets the following requirements:

   o  The RRSIG owner name is equal to the RRset owner name.

   o  The RRSIG class is equal to the RRset class.

   o  The RRSIG Type Covered field is equal to the RRset type.

   o  The RRSIG Original TTL field is equal to the TTL of the RRset.

   o  The RRSIG RR's TTL is equal to the TTL of the RRset.

   o  The RRSIG Labels field is equal to the number of labels in the
      RRset owner name, not counting the null root label and not
      counting the leftmost label if it is a wildcard.

   o  The RRSIG Signer's Name field is equal to the name of the zone
      containing the RRset.

   o  The RRSIG Algorithm, Signer's Name, and Key Tag fields identify a
      zone key DNSKEY record at the zone apex.
requirements.condition: For each authoritative RRset in a signed zone.
requirements.required_behavior: There MUST be at least one associated RRSIG record that satisfies all of the listed RRSIG requirements together.
requirements.why_checkable: For each authoritative RRset, the zone can be checked for at least one RRSIG that simultaneously satisfies the listed predicates; separate records satisfying different predicates do not suffice.

requirements.why_checkable: Compare the required RRSIG owner name with the covered RRset owner name.

requirements.quote:
An RRset MAY have multiple RRSIG RRs
   associated with it.
requirements.required_behavior: The RRset MAY have multiple associated RRSIG RRs; multiple signatures are permitted, not required.
requirements.why_checkable: A zone can contain more than one RRSIG for one RRset without violating the signature-count constraint.

requirements.quote:
Note that as RRSIG RRs are closely tied to the
   RRsets whose signatures they contain, RRSIG RRs, unlike all other DNS



Arends, et al.              Standards Track                     [Page 5]


RFC 4035             DNSSEC Protocol Modifications            March 2005


   RR types, do not form RRsets.  In particular, the TTL values among
   RRSIG RRs with a common owner name do not follow the RRset rules
   described in [RFC2181].
requirements.condition: When representing or grouping RRSIG RRs.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat RRSIG RRs as forming RRsets.
requirements.why_checkable: The RRSIG grouping or storage logic can be inspected to determine whether these records are treated as an RRset.

requirements.quote:
In particular, the TTL values among
   RRSIG RRs with a common owner name do not follow the RRset rules
   described in [RFC2181].
requirements.condition: When RRSIG RRs have a common owner name.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Apply the ordinary RRset TTL rules referenced in this passage to those RRSIG TTL values solely because the RRSIG RRs share an owner name.
requirements.why_checkable: The TTL handling path can be inspected for application of ordinary RRset TTL rules to a group of RRSIG records sharing an owner name.

requirements.quote:
An RRSIG RR itself MUST NOT be signed, as signing an RRSIG RR would
   add no value and would create an infinite loop in the signing
   process.
requirements.condition: When signing a zone and considering an RRSIG RR itself.
requirements.why_checkable: Generated signatures and signing eligibility logic can be checked for attempts to sign RRSIG records.

requirements.quote:
The NS RRset that appears at the zone apex name MUST be signed, but
   the NS RRsets that appear at delegation points (that is, the NS
   RRsets in the parent zone that delegate the name to the child zone's
   name servers) MUST NOT be signed.  Glue address RRsets associated
   with delegations MUST NOT be signed.
requirements.condition: For the NS RRset at the zone apex in a signed zone.
requirements.required_behavior: The zone-apex NS RRset MUST be signed.
requirements.why_checkable: Inspect the zone-apex NS RRset for a covering signature.

requirements.quote:
An RRSIG RR itself MUST NOT be signed, as signing an RRSIG RR would
   add no value and would create an infinite loop in the signing
   process.

   The NS RRset that appears at the zone apex name MUST be signed, but
   the NS RRsets that appear at delegation points (that is, the NS
   RRsets in the parent zone that delegate the name to the child zone's
   name servers) MUST NOT be signed.  Glue address RRsets associated
   with delegations MUST NOT be signed.

   There MUST be an RRSIG for each RRset using at least one DNSKEY of
   each algorithm in the zone apex DNSKEY RRset.  The apex DNSKEY RRset
   itself MUST be signed by each algorithm appearing in the DS RRset
   located at the delegating parent (if any).
requirements.condition: For each RRset subject to signing in the signed zone; the RRSIG, delegation-point NS, and delegation-glue signing prohibitions in this section remain applicable.
requirements.required_behavior: There MUST be an RRSIG for the RRset using at least one DNSKEY of each algorithm present in the zone-apex DNSKEY RRset.
requirements.why_checkable: For each RRset to be signed, compare the algorithms represented in its signatures with the algorithms of the zone-apex DNSKEY records and verify the signing keys.

requirements.quote:
There MUST be an RRSIG for each RRset using at least one DNSKEY of
   each algorithm in the zone apex DNSKEY RRset.  The apex DNSKEY RRset
   itself MUST be signed by each algorithm appearing in the DS RRset
   located at the delegating parent (if any).
requirements.condition: For the apex DNSKEY RRset, when a DS RRset is located at the delegating parent.
requirements.required_behavior: The apex DNSKEY RRset MUST be signed by each algorithm appearing in the parent DS RRset.
requirements.why_checkable: Compare the algorithm values in the parent DS RRset with the signature algorithms covering the child apex DNSKEY RRset.
